sections.html:
Decatur sits on Wheeler Lake, a stretch of the Tennessee River in north Alabama. Morgan County's largest city and its seat, Decatur also reaches across the river into Limestone County, in a small area between U.S. 31 and I-65. The 2020 census counted 57,938 residents. Huntsville is about 25 miles northeast and Birmingham 86 miles south.

Locals divide town into four quadrants. The CSX main line splits east from west, and Moulton Street splits north from south. That grid matters when you describe a house, because street patterns, zoning and building styles differ from one side of the tracks to the other.

Two towns were joined to make today's Decatur. The original city grew around a ferry landing and the first railroad west of the Appalachians. A second town, New Decatur, was founded in 1887 west of the tracks, renamed Albany in 1916 and merged with Decatur in 1925. Old Decatur and Albany still appear as neighborhood names on the northeast side. The city also claims the largest Victorian-era home district in Alabama.

Owners of century-old houses often face roof, wiring, foundation and plumbing questions that scare off buyers who need a bank loan. Neighborhood groupings buyers recognize:

  • Older core: Old Decatur, Albany, Downtown and the riverfront Harborview area.
  • Southeast: Point Mallard Estates, Indian Hills, Burningtree Mountain, Cedar Lake and Hickory Hills.
  • Southwest: Westmeade, Austinville, Oak Lea, Moulton Heights and Autumn Ridge, among many subdivisions.

If your house is in the older core, collect whatever records you have: receipts for roof, wiring or plumbing work, permits and any inspection reports. Buyers of older houses want proof of what has been replaced, and a folder of papers answers questions before they turn into price cuts. Where records are missing, say so plainly and let the buyer decide how to price the unknowns.

Humid subtropical weather means about 53.4 inches of rain yearly and 51 to 52 days at or above 90 degrees. Severe storms bring damaging wind, large hail and tornado risk, mostly in spring, with a second severe season that peaks in November. Remnants of Gulf hurricanes sometimes bring strong wind or heavy rain between July and October.

  • Roof age and any hail or wind damage that was never repaired.
  • Gutters, grading and crawlspace moisture after a rainy December, the wettest month on average.
  • Water staining around chimneys, skylights and window frames.
  • Air conditioning age, since summers are hot and humid.

A house with an open insurance claim or deferred storm repairs can stall on an ordinary listing. A cash buyer prices those repairs in and skips the insurer's underwriting.

Most commutes run on U.S. 31 (6th Avenue), U.S. 72 Alternate (State Route 20), State Route 24 and State Route 67, which includes the Beltline Road that partly circles the city. I-65 passes east of town, and I-565 begins northeast of Decatur and connects to Huntsville. The twin-span Steamboat Bill Memorial Bridge carries U.S. 31 and U.S. 72 Alternate across the river. Huntsville International and Pryor Field Regional are the two nearby airports.

Public transit is limited. NARCOG Transit runs demand-response service, and there is no fixed-route bus. A buyer without a car has few options, so a house's distance from the main roads is worth mentioning.

sections.h2: Steps to sell a house in Decatur
sections.html:
Closing happens once the probate judge records the deed, and Alabama wants the recordation tax paid before it will accept one. Alabama Code section 40-22-1 sets that tax at 50 cents for every $500 of value conveyed, and a form swearing to the real purchase price goes with the deed.

Morgan County's probate office handles most Decatur parcels, but the part of the city in Limestone County records there. Find out which county holds your parcel before signing anything. The usual sequence:

  1. Collect the deed, a mortgage payoff statement if you owe one and a list of known repairs.
  2. Settle who must sign. That means each owner on the deed, and a personal representative for any owner who has died.
  3. Hire a closing agent to search the title and draw up the closing statement.
  4. Liens and unpaid property tax get paid from the proceeds.
  5. The deed is then recorded with the probate judge.

Bills are due October 1, and unpaid ones turn delinquent after December 31. The rule is the same whether your Decatur parcel is in Morgan or Limestone County. Selling in fall or winter? Ask the closing agent how that year's bill will be handled. If it is already due, proceeds can pay it at the table. A prior year left unpaid may become a lien, and a buyer will want it cleared before taking title. Ask the county office for current balances, since the closing agent will need them to prepare the settlement statement.

sections.h2: When a job move forces a quick sale
sections.html:
A plant announcement or a layoff can uproot a family quickly, and the local housing market tends to follow hiring at industrial employers. Owners with a transfer or a new job tied to a plant or the Huntsville area sometimes have little time. If that describes you, fix your deadline first and work backward to see what each route allows.

A listing needs weeks of showings, an inspection and a lender's appraisal, and the closing hangs on the buyer's loan. Paying cash avoids the appraisal gap, so the calendar can run faster. Either route needs a closing agent, a clear title and a settled tax bill, so begin with those items even before you pick a buyer.

sections.h2: What Decatur sellers usually run into
sections.html:
Age, repairs and timing cause most of the trouble. Decatur has a long housing history, and people who own older houses tend to postpone big jobs until moving day.

  • Inherited houses whose heirs live in other states and want no part of managing repairs.
  • Rentals with worn-out units and tenants who are hard to move out.
  • Houses with storm damage, old roofs or deferred repairs.
  • Owners facing a job change tied to a plant or the Huntsville area.

Title work stays with a cash sale, yet showings, appraisal gaps and repair negotiations can go. If that suits you, the form on this page is the fastest way to begin.

faqs.q: How many people live in Decatur, Alabama?
faqs.a: The 2020 census recorded 57,938 residents. Most of the city is in Morgan County, with a small part in Limestone County.

faqs.q: Do I pay a tax to record my deed in Decatur?
faqs.a: Yes. The recordation tax is 50 cents per $500 of value, paid before the probate judge will record the deed. The closing agent normally collects it on the closing statement.

faqs.q: When is property tax due on a Decatur house?
faqs.a: Due October 1, late after December 31. The closing statement usually divides the current year's bill between buyer and seller.

faqs.q: Which county records a Decatur deed?
faqs.a: Most of Decatur is in Morgan County, so most deeds go to that county's probate office. A small part north of the river is in Limestone County, so confirm where your parcel lies.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Decatur house with storm or roof damage?
faqs.a: Yes. Hail and wind come in spring and again in November, and damaged houses sell regularly. A cash buyer looks at the house as it is, so repairs need not come first.
